description.value: A 30-site regional campground on the northern tip of Malcolm Island, reached by BC Ferries from Port McNeill then a short paved ride to a dramatic coastal headland celebrated as one of BC's best spots to watch orcas from shore during summer salmon runs; pit toilets and reservations available.

raw_osm.description: Moderate to steep cobble beach. Drift logs, kelp. Developed. Non-potable water at tap. Boat launch (high water only). Hiking trail to whale rubbing beach, viewing platform. Hydrophones.
raw_osm.name: Bere Point Regional Park Campground

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM description tag is the richest evidence source, explicitly stating 'Non-potable water at tap' (corroborated by drinking_water=no) and 'Developed', while reservation=yes confirms reservations are accepted. The fetched website content rendered only RDMW navigation menus with no campground-specific body text, so the OSM tags are the primary factual source for all amenity fields. Most optional amenities cannot be confirmed or denied from available evidence, and the second URL (bcmarinetrails.org) was not fetched.
concerns: Website content fetched but rendered only site-wide navigation menus — no campground-specific body text was captured, severely limiting amenity verification beyond OSM tags
A secondary URL (https://www.bcmarinetrails.org/map_site/bere-point) is present in OSM url tag but was not fetched; it may contain additional amenity detail

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate developed regional park campground with 30 sites and reservations on Malcolm Island; useful for touring cyclists exploring this remote part of northern Vancouver Island.
